text: Confirm the service's own status: `systemctl status apiworker`. It's `active` and not crash-looping -- so this isn't like a typical broken-config crash. Check its journal: `journalctl -u apiworker -n 30`. It repeats 'cannot open connection N/40: Too many open files' -- that's EMFILE, a file-descriptor ceiling, not a code bug.

Get its actual PID (`systemctl show apiworker --property=MainPID`) and compare the limit the kernel is enforcing on it against what it's actually holding: `cat /proc/<pid>/limits | grep 'open files'` vs `ls /proc/<pid>/fd | wc -l`. The usage is pinned right at the limit, well short of 40.

Unlike a plain app-level ulimit, this service's fd ceiling comes from the unit file itself: `systemctl cat apiworker` shows a `LimitNOFILE=` line under `[Service]`. A recent hardening pass set it far below what this service has always legitimately needed -- the app has no leak, the ceiling is just wrong.

Edit the unit (`sudo systemctl edit --full apiworker` or edit `/etc/systemd/system/apiworker.service` directly) and raise `LimitNOFILE` to something like `4096`. Then `sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl restart apiworker` -- a running unit's limits don't change without a restart, since the limit is applied at process launch.
